Class QuestsAPI

java.lang.Object
com.atomictempest.quests.api.QuestsAPI
public final class QuestsAPI extends Object
The Quests mod, for other plugins: add your own kinds of goals, count progress, read and add achievements and quests, and hear when a player finishes one. Declare "AtomicTempest:Quests": "*" under Dependencies (or OptionalDependencies, and check isAvailable()) in your manifest.json. 
// In your plugin's setup():
QuestsAPI.registerObjective("fishing:catch", "Catch fish", "Catch", "fish", true, "Fish id or part of it. Empty: any fish.");
// Whenever a player catches a fish:
QuestsAPI.progress(playerUuid, "fishing:catch", fishItemId, 1);
Everything here is safe to call from any thread.

    • isAvailable

      public static boolean isAvailable()
      True once the Quests mod has started. Everything else does nothing (or returns empty) until then.

    • registerObjective

      public static ObjectiveType registerObjective(String id, String label, String verb, String noun, boolean usesTarget, String hint)
      Adds a kind of goal that admins can pick in the editor. Count it with progress(UUID, String, String, long). Register again after a restart (in your setup); goals made with it are kept while your mod is missing, but do not count.
      Parameters:
      id - unique, "modname:what", such as "fishing:catch"
      label - the editor's button, such as "Catch fish"
      verb - the start of a made-up description, such as "Catch" ("Catch 10 fish.")
      noun - what is counted, plural, such as "fish"
      usesTarget - true if admins can narrow it to one thing ("Which one"), matched as part of the subject you pass to progress(UUID, String, String, long)
      hint - one line explaining "Which one", or ""

    • progress

      public static void progress(UUID player, String objectiveId, String subject, long amount)
      Counts progress for every enabled goal of this objective that the subject matches. Works for the built-in objectives too (such as "KILL" with a mob name), if your mod does something the game does not report.
      Parameters:
      subject - what was done, matched against the goal's "Which one" (a block, mob, item or fish id); may be null
      amount - how many; 0 or less does nothing

    • trigger

      public static void trigger(UUID player, String trigger, long amount)
      Fires a named trigger: every "Custom trigger" goal whose "Which one" is this name (ignoring case) counts up. The same as the Quests_Trigger interaction and the /questtrigger command.
